issue.title: A malformed assets declaration passes flow validation and is then silently dropped at runtime

relevant_locations.role: Runtime asset processing and escalation logic

llm_context.input_title: A malformed assets declaration passes flow validation and is then silently dropped at runtime
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: A malformed assets declaration in a Kestra flow passes flow validation because the underlying `AssetsDeclaration` model class lacks Bean Validation annotations. At runtime, asset failures default to `WARN`, causing the malformed declaration to be silently downgraded and dropped without emitting any lineage or errors.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The model class `AssetsDeclaration` (`core/src/main/java/io/kestra/core/models/assets/AssetsDeclaration.java`) does not have validation annotations such as `@Valid`, `@NotNull`, or `@NotEmpty`. Consequently, flow validators do not inspect or constrain its contents, and runtime asset processing defaults to `WARN` rather than failing hard or logging a hard error when a declaration fails to render or emit.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect AssetsDeclaration validation annotations
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect AssetsDeclaration in core/src/main/java/io/kestra/core/models/assets/AssetsDeclaration.java and verify the absence of Bean Validation annotations.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add validation annotations to AssetsDeclaration
step_by_step_plan.description: Add appropriate Bean Validation annotations (such as @NotNull, @NotBlank, or @Valid) to the fields of AssetsDeclaration to enforce correct structure during flow validation.

step_by_step_plan.title: Review runtime asset processing in ExecutorService
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect io.kestra.executor.ExecutorService in executor/src/main/java/io/kestra/executor/ExecutorService.java to ensure asset processing failure handling does not silently downgrade malformed declarations to WARN without proper reporting.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add regression test and execute verification suite
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a unit or integration test validating that a flow with a malformed assets declaration fails validation, and execute the test command to verify the fix.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Declarative constraints placed on class fields (such as `@NotNull`, `@NotEmpty`, or `@Valid`) that frameworks use to validate model instances automatically.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Without validation annotations, malformed configurations or input blocks are accepted blindly by the validation engine.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Adding validation annotations to `AssetsDeclaration` will ensure that flow validation rejects invalid asset blocks before execution begins.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: How an application handles errors during execution, such as whether it fails fast or gracefully logs a warning.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: A default behavior of `WARN` hides issues by allowing executions to turn green despite failures in optional or declared auxiliary features.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The issue notes that asset processing defaults to `WARN`, which contributes to the silent dropping of malformed asset declarations.

common_pitfalls: Forgetting to import validation packages from `jakarta.validation.constraints` or `jakarta.validation`.
Modifying runtime execution logic when the primary requirement is flow validation annotation support.
